symptom: The C-02 deconstruction stub and node badge exist in the production canvas, but their legacy data-deconstruct-* attributes do not match the canonical data-decon-node-* anchors in the Agent UI testspec and coverage matrix.
direct_cause: NodeDeconstructionBadge and the deconstruction Electron walkthrough copied the older video-deconstruction selectors while the generated Agent UI contract declared data-decon-node-stub and data-decon-node-badge.
class_root: The production selector owner was not required to use the generated design-contract anchor, so a renamed selector could silently become a coverage drift entry instead of a contract failure.
affected_population: Users reaching the deconstruction collapsed state on a generation-canvas video node
C-02 Agent UI conformance and deconstruction-panel walkthroughs
Any future selector rename in a design-contract anchor without a production structure assertion
entry_points: NodeDeconstructionBadge renders the source-node collapsed stub and badge
deconstruction-panel.walk.mjs locates those anchors during the C-02 state transition
check-agent-ui-coverage validates source selectors against generated design anchors
internal_only_reason: The selector names are Nomi's internal generated design-contract and runtime test boundary; no third-party documentation defines them.
invariants: Every production C-02 deconstruction node stub uses data-decon-node-stub.
Every production C-02 deconstruction node badge uses data-decon-node-badge.
The real walkthrough and coverage matrix query the same canonical anchors, and the legacy data-deconstruct-* selectors are absent from the production owner.
generality_proof: The canonical attributes are enforced at the only production owner for these two C-02 elements, while both independent consumers—the Electron walkthrough and the coverage matrix—are updated to the same generated contract. The structure test fails if either selector drifts or the old alias returns.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the canonical runtime anchors for the collapsed deconstruction stub and node badge.

shared_boundaries.symbol: keeps the C-02 deconstruction node anchors canonical
shared_boundaries.responsibility: Fail closed when a canonical C-02 anchor is removed or a legacy selector is reintroduced.
Validate that the matrix source selector exists in the production file and matches the uncovered generated anchor.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both locators now use data-decon-node-stub and data-decon-node-badge, matching the production owner and testspec.
The generated extractor already declares data-decon-node-stub and data-decon-node-badge; no alternate selector source is needed or changed.

recurrence.reason: Selector drift can recur for any design-contract anchor when production markup and independent walkthrough consumers are edited without a shared structural assertion.
same_class_scan: Searched all src, tests, scripts, and docs paths for data-deconstruct-stub, data-deconstruct-result-badge, data-decon-node-stub, and data-decon-node-badge.
Checked the sole production owner NodeDeconstructionBadge.tsx, the Electron deconstruction walkthrough, the generated extractor, and the coverage gate matrix.
Confirmed the generated design spec and testspec already use the canonical data-decon-node-* names, so the repair is a convergence change rather than a contract rename.

prevention.invariant: The production owner contains both canonical C-02 selectors and contains neither legacy selector.
prevention.failure_mode: Vitest fails before the walkthrough or coverage gate can report a misleading drift state.
prevention.strategy: Keep the canonical names in the generated contract and enforce them at the production owner with a structure test; make all independent consumers query those same names.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old data-deconstruct-* aliases are deleted from the production owner and the real walkthrough; retaining either changed path as a compatibility alias would violate the single canonical selector contract.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls this internal DOM selector contract.

migration: No persisted data is affected. Existing running walkthroughs must use the canonical selectors after the next build; no compatibility alias is retained because the old selectors were test-only contract drift.
residual_risks: The coverage matrix still records these anchors as runtime-present-unmeasured because the general Agent conformance walk does not drive the full deconstruction fixture; the dedicated deconstruction walkthrough remains the behavioral evidence.
A real Electron C-02 run still depends on the deconstruction fixture and media path; this patch does not claim that paid or provider-backed generation is certified.
